'''''Photinia davidiana''''', the '''Chinese photinia''',<ref>{{PLANTS|symbol=PHDA5|taxon=Photinia davidiana|accessdate=12 July  2018}}</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Rosaceae]]. It is a shrub or tree native to Asia, ranging from central and southern China to northern Vietnam, Taiwan, northern Sumatra, and [[Mount Kinabalu]] on [[Borneo]].<ref name = powo/> Its flowers are white and grow in close clusters, followed by small [[pome]] fruits. 

It is grown as an [[ornamental plant]], and has been introduced to [[North America]] as a garden plant.

Two varieties are accepted.<ref name = powo/>
*''Photinia davidiana'' var. ''davidiana'' – central and southern China, northern Vietnam, Taiwan, northern Sumatra, and Mount Kinabalu
*''Photinia davidiana'' var. ''undulata'' {{small|(Decne.) Long Y.Wang, W.Guo & W.B.Liao}} – central and southern China and northern Vietnam

The species was first described as ''Stranvaesia davidiana'' by [[Joseph Decaisne]] in 1874. In 2019 it was placed in genus ''[[Photinia]]'' as ''Photinia davidiana''.<ref name = powo/>
